## Part 1 · 00:03

[00:03] Did you know ancient Jews and Christians didn't look forward to going to heaven as much as God bringing heaven to earth? Many modern people think of apocalypticism as though it's about expectations of cinematic suffering and the total destruction of the world or universe while the righteous go to heaven. But for ancient Jews and Christians, apocalypticism starts with the conviction that because God is just, everyone is ultimately going to get what they deserve. But these thinkers also weren't blind to the astonishing injustice of this world.

[00:42] And when they observed righteous people being persecuted and even executed for their pious lives, they concluded that God will bring justice at a future time when the righteous will be resurrected to receive their rewards while the wicked oppressors finally get what they deserve, too. In other words, they were looking forward to the day when God would bring heaven's justice to earth, radically rebooting a broken world and restoring cosmic programming to factory settings. In my course, Visions of the End, we explore the vivid ancient prophecies underlying these expectations.

[01:17] You will gain a rich historical toolkit to recognize the narrative roots of apocalyptic end times expectations, decode apocalyptic language, and understand the political influences and implications of early Jewish and Christian expectations of the end times. I hope you'll join me as we uncover the fascinating history of the end times.
